title: Integral stratified lfp constructibility agrees with finite constant local models
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension, $A=\mathcal O_E$ its valuation ring [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and $X$ a Noetherian scheme, meaning quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Give $A$ its valuation topology and put $B_X=p_X^*\underline A$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] on the small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $M$ be a sheaf of $B_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The following conditions are equivalent:

(i) $M$ is constructible in the general ring-object sense [def-sfb-constructible-module]: it admits a finite constructible locally closed stratification [def-constructible-stratification] on every stratum $T$ of which its restriction is locally finitely presented over $B_T$ [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented]. Thus on a pro-étale covering of $T$ it is the cokernel of a morphism $B_V^m\to B_V^n$ for finite nonnegative integers $m,n$; the matrix entries are arbitrary sections of $B_V$.

(ii) $M$ is constructible in the finite constant local model sense [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: it admits a finite constructible locally closed stratification on every stratum $T$ of which there is a pro-étale covering $\{V_j\to T\}$ and finitely presented scalar $A$-modules $P_j$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] with
$$M|_{V_j}\cong B_{V_j}\otimes_A P_j.$$
Here $A$ and $P_j$ denote constant sheaves, and the tensor is extension along the constant-section map $A\to B_{V_j}$. Finitely presented means that $P_j$ is a cokernel of a scalar matrix $A^{u_j}\to A^{v_j}$ of finite size. The stratifications in (i) and (ii) may differ. Torsion scalar modules are allowed. No completeness, finite-dimension, separatedness, finite-type or invertibility assumption is imposed beyond the stated Noetherian hypothesis on $X$.

source.place: Hemo–Richarz–Scholbach Example 3.1 (continuous-function coefficient rings), Theorem 4.13 (pro-étale-local perfect-constant characterization), Theorem 6.2(2) (the lisse heart consists of finitely presented scalar local models), Theorem 6.2(3) (the constructible heart), Lemma 6.10 and Corollary 6.11(1) (t-admissibility for the valuation ring), and Theorem 6.12(2) (regular coherence of continuous-function rings). Compare Bhatt–Scholze Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(3). The local-finite-presentation-to-perfect step is part of this coefficient-specific comparison obligation, not a verbatim consequence of the cited heart characterization.

proof.text: We first prove a local statement on each stratum, keeping its actual immersion into $X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], every nonempty family of closed subsets of $|X|$ has a minimal member. Applied to the complements of an increasing chain of opens, minimality forces that chain to stabilize, so $|X|$ is Noetherian. Every subspace $|T|$ is also Noetherian: for an increasing chain $O_j$ of subspace opens choose ambient opens $U_j$ with $O_j=U_j\cap|T|$; the ambient opens $H_j=\bigcup_{k\leq j}U_k$ form an increasing chain and satisfy $H_j\cap|T|=O_j$, so their stabilization gives stabilization of $O_j$. Thus the topological hypothesis of the descent lemma used below holds on every stratum, irrespective of its chosen scheme structure. Suppose (i), choose its finite stratification, and fix one stratum $T$. By [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented] and the finite-biproduct cokernel definition [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module], $M_T=M|_T$ has a pro-étale cover $(V_i\to T)$ with presentations $B_{V_i}^{m_i}\xrightarrow{F_i}B_{V_i}^{n_i}\to M_T|_{V_i}\to0$. Inverse image along any further scheme map preserves these finite presentations: [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] identifies the coefficient rings and makes module pullback exact. The site definition says each $V_i\to T$ is flat and the family is jointly surjective on points.

source.place: Definition 01OV (definition-noetherian) and Lemma 01OZ (lemma-Noetherian-topology), via the cited minimal-closed-subset node; the subspace ACC argument is written out.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations] with the topological ring $A=\mathcal O_E$. It is totally disconnected in its valuation topology (balls are clopen), so that comparison is an isomorphism and identifies $B_{V_i}$ with the sheaf $U\mapsto C(|U|,A)$, naturally under restriction. The entries of $F_i$ are continuous functions on $|V_i|$: a map from a finite free module is determined by the images of its standard generators, whose coordinates lie in $B_{V_i}(V_i)$. For each $v\in |V_i|$ define the scalar module $Q_{i,v}=A^{n_i}/F_i(v)(A^{m_i})$. Encode its isomorphism class in the fixed set $\mathcal S$ of isomorphism classes of all finite scalar matrix cokernels (a quotient of the set of finite matrices over $A$). Write $r_i(v)=[Q_{i,v}]$. Each entry is equal at comparable points of $V_i$: a continuous map sends a specialization to a specialization, while in the Hausdorff space $A$ comparable points are equal. Hence $r_i$ is specialization invariant. This uses the integral continuous ring itself, not the rationalization. The integral coefficient ring used in the entry-pullback lemma below is exactly this $B$: [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients] uses the valuation subring $\{x\in E:\lVert x\rVert\leq1\}$ with its subspace topology and pulls back its condensed continuous-function ring. For this finite extension, the norm is the same valuation absolute value defining $A$ in the item.

source.place: Example 3.1: continuous-function coefficient realization; specialization invariance follows directly from the Hausdorff topology.

proof.text: The functions $r_i$ agree over equal base points, including across distinct presentations. Indeed, if $v\in V_i$ and $w\in V_j$ lie over $x\in T$, apply [lem-weil-common-extension-fields] to $\kappa(v)/\kappa(x)$ and $\kappa(w)/\kappa(x)$ to obtain compatible embeddings into a field $K$. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $K$ by [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique]. The embeddings into $\Omega$ give maps $a:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V_i$ and $b:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V_j$ by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field]. Their composites to $T$ correspond to the same pair consisting of $x$ and the common embedding $\kappa(x)\to\Omega$, so the same bijection proves that they are equal. Thus they define a map to $V_i\times_T V_j$, in agreement with Stacks Tag 01JT, schemes.tex, lemma-points-fibre-product [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points]. Exact module inverse image and Cartesian coefficients [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] pull both presentations back to presentations of the same module $M_\Omega$. Under [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-field-proetale-evaluation], evaluation at $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ preserves cokernels and finite free modules. Its coefficient ring is $A$, by [det-pe-condensed-point-coefficients] at the one-point profinite set. [lem-weil-pbc-integral-regular-coefficient-pullback], applied to each entry as an endomorphism of the regular module in the standard bases, identifies the pulled matrix entries with $F_i(v)$ and $F_j(w)$; a continuous function on the one-point underlying space of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ has exactly this value. Consequently both $Q_{i,v}$ and $Q_{j,w}$ are isomorphic to the same scalar module $M_\Omega(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega)$, so $r_i(v)=r_j(w)$. Neither conservativity of geometric points nor finite-dimensionality of the integral modules is asserted.

source.place: Examples 4.1.10 and 4.2.11; geometric-field evaluation. Common field and its algebraic closure use Stacks 0H7K (fields.tex, lemma-common-extension-field) and 09GT (fields.tex, theorem-existence-algebraic-closure); field-valued points use 01J9 and 01JT (schemes.tex, lemma-characterize-points and lemma-points-fibre-product).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-field-rank-descent] to the scheme $T$, the flat jointly surjective family $(V_i\to T)$ of step 1, the set $\mathcal S$, and the functions $r_i$. Its statement allows any target type, not merely natural-number ranks. Steps 2 and 3 verify respectively specialization invariance and compatibility over equal base points. It gives a locally constant function $d:|T|\to\mathcal S$ with $r_i=d\circ|V_i\to T|$. In particular each $r_i$ is locally constant because scheme morphisms are continuous. This is the point where Noetherianity is essential; the source members $V_i$ need not be Noetherian.

source.place: Example 3.1; agent specialization-invariant descent argument, using the existing general descent statement for arbitrary target sets.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $A$ is a DVR and has a uniformizer $\pi$. Apply [lem-sfb-continuous-integral-matrix-local-smith] to $Y=|V_i|$ and the continuous matrix $F_i$ of step 2, whose scalar cokernel class is locally constant by step 4. It supplies an open cover $(W_{i\alpha})$ with continuous invertible row and column matrices and a fixed scalar rectangular diagonal matrix $D_{i\alpha}$, satisfying $L F_i R=D_{i\alpha}$. Regard each open as its open subscheme. Through [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations], those matrices and their inverses are actual mutually inverse sheaf maps on $W_{i\alpha}$, since matrix multiplication is pointwise multiplication of continuous sections. Thus the presentation of $M$ on that open is isomorphic to the presentation by $D_{i\alpha}$. Put $P_{i\alpha}=\operatorname{coker}(D_{i\alpha}:A^{m_i}\to A^{n_i})$; it is finitely presented by [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. The scalar tensor universal property identifies the sheaf cokernel of $D_{i\alpha}$ with $B_{W_{i\alpha}}\otimes_A P_{i\alpha}$: a map from either object to a $B$-module $N$ is exactly a tuple of $n_i$ local sections of $N$ annihilating the columns of $D_{i\alpha}$, with agreement and gluing on overlaps. This is also the coequalizer definition of relative tensor in [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. No flatness of $B$ as a constant $A$-module is required. Open covers are pro-étale covers, and cover composition [sk-def-pe-site] makes the family $(W_{i\alpha}\to T)$ a pro-étale cover. We have therefore obtained the required finite scalar local models on every original stratum. The original finite stratification proves (ii).

source.place: Example 3.1 and continuous integral pivot arguments in Theorem 6.12(2); agent local constant-type Smith argument, followed by the explicit tensor/cokernel universal-property calculation.

proof.text: Conversely assume (ii). On each given stratum and each model open $V_j$, take the finite scalar presentation $A^{u_j}\xrightarrow{G_j}A^{v_j}\to P_j\to0$ supplied by [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. For any sheaf of $B_{V_j}$-modules $N$, a $B_{V_j}$-linear map $B_{V_j}\otimes_A P_j\to N$ is, by the relative tensor coequalizer [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor], exactly an $A$-linear map from the constant sheaf $P_j$ to $N$. Giving this map is giving $v_j$ sections $t_1,\ldots,t_{v_j}\in N(V_j)$ satisfying $\sum_{b=1}^{v_j}(G_j)_{ba}t_b=0$ for every $1\leq a\leq u_j$: the sections are the images of the scalar generators, and these equations impose their scalar relations; restriction and sheaf gluing give the unique map on the associated constant sheaf. Those tuples are also exactly the $B_{V_j}$-linear maps $B_{V_j}^{v_j}\to N$ annihilating $G_j$. This proves the cokernel universal property and hence the presentation $B_{V_j}^{u_j}\xrightarrow{G_j}B_{V_j}^{v_j}\to B_{V_j}\otimes_A P_j\to0$. Transport it through the assumed local-model isomorphism to obtain a finite presentation of $M|_{V_j}$ in exactly the sense of [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. The definition [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented] now applies on each stratum, and the given finite constructible stratification is a witness to [def-sfb-constructible-module]. Hence (i). This direction does not use Noetherianity. The empty scheme uses the empty stratification; zero modules use the zero matrix. The diagonal description in step 5 includes $A/\pi^e$ for $e\geq1$, so no torsion-free hypothesis has entered either direction.

split_report.summary: Proved the comparison by continuous integral matrices, common geometric-fibre scalar cokernel types, descent of specialization-invariant functions through flat covers, and continuous local Smith elimination. Reused existing continuous realization, geometric-field evaluation, Cartesian coefficients and arbitrary-type descent statements. Added only the topological integral matrix lemma, statement-only. Preserved the entire statement, including torsion, general local finite presentation, arbitrary Noetherian schemes and absence of completeness or invertibility assumptions.
split_report.blueprint: lem-sfb-dc-hom-preserves.proof.md, first sentence 'use the characterisation of bounded constructible complexes recalled in the proof of [lem-sfb-dc-lower-star-preserves]': matching the general-lfp predicate of the statement with the scalar-model characterisation (parent steps 1, 3, 4, 5). Steps 1-5 provide the general-lfp to scalar-model bridge in that sentence; step 6 proves the converse. This is below the unit restricted-functor step, not a replacement of its route.

tool_uses.why: Generic coefficient realization for totally disconnected topological rings; needed to read integral presentation entries as continuous functions. The restricted-functor unit gives no such theorem.
Generic exact evaluation at a geometric field; compares scalar cokernels without any conservativity assertion. The unit has no geometric evaluation theorem.
Its statement permits arbitrary target types and descends scalar module isomorphism classes; this generic topological flat-descent tool is not in the restricted-functor unit.
Generic arithmetic result giving the DVR and uniformizer needed by integral Smith elimination.

Explicit pointwise formula for pulled-back integral regular-module coefficients; used entrywise to compare scalar matrices, rather than assuming a naturality clause absent from a realization statement.

Generic exact coefficient-preserving module pullback for integral coefficients, needed for finite presentations and geometric evaluation; no restricted-functor statement supplies this underived comparison.
Generic coefficient normalization at the one-point profinite set identifies evaluated integral coefficients with A; this is a point-site tool, not a replacement of the unit route.
Generic field-amalgamation lemma supplies compatible residue-field embeddings for the comparison of two presentations over one base point; the restricted-functor unit supplies no such field theorem.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q29-01db7b331 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item, the new node lem-sfb-continuous-integral-matrix-local-smith, the unit sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors, the first sentence of the ancestor lem-sfb-dc-hom-preserves proof, and the statements of all 26 cited nodes. HRS checked at Example 3.1, Theorem 6.2(2)/(3), Remark 6.4, Lemma 6.10/Corollary 6.11 and the Theorem 6.12(2) proof (the pivot/division step f=a·h). The coefficient ring p_X^*C(-,O_E) is the same object in the sfb and pbc chapters: the pullback from the point uses the same Lan/LC(S,Z) construction, and for finite E the topology on O_E is its valuation topology. No SGA source is cited. Step 1: |X| is Noetherian by the minimal-closed-subset leaf, and the subspace ACC argument (H_j∩T=O_j) is correct; Cartesian coefficients give exact pullback of presentations; covers are flat and jointly surjective. Step 2: O_E is totally disconnected, so the realization lemma applies; matrix entries are continuous, and specialization invariance holds because A is T1. Step 3: common extension field and algebraic closure give a=b over T. Geometric-field evaluation, point coefficients and integral-regular-coefficient-pullback then give Q_{i,v}≅M_Ω(Ω)≅Q_{j,w} as full A-modules, so torsion is kept. The fibre-product citation is redundant but harmless. Step 4: the rank-descent statement allows any target type; all its hypotheses come from steps 1-3. Step 5: Smith is applied only after local constancy. Continuous L,R are mutually inverse sheaf automorphisms. coker D≅B⊗_A P follows from the universal property (Hom from constant P_W equals Hom_A(P,N(W))), with no flatness needed, and the composed open/pro-étale covers are pro-étale covers. Step 6: the converse by explicit generators and relations is correct. New node is true, by an independent check: with m,n fixed, the cokernel class fixes the Smith list; the minimal-valuation pivot set is open; dividing by p is continuous and stays in A; structure-theorem cancellation drives the induction. Tested on Y empty, m=0 or n=0, F=0, F=(π^a), F=(1), and mixed rectangular cases; F(y)=y on {0}∪{π^k} is correctly excluded. It is a topological lemma strictly smaller than the item, not a clause of it. Duplicate candidates opened and rejected: scalar DVR Smith, field matrix elimination, pivot/analytic covers, the four integral-lfp torsion/resolution nodes, condensed-lfp-local-triviality, det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model. No cycle; proof_deps equals the union of step uses; blueprint from/via/same_as are correct.
